summary: A target-level completion of the NC.3 planning pass. Imports the accepted parent’s continuous nonabelian cocycles, twists, torsors, exactness and finite-quotient work, adds the positive continuous H2 obstruction bridge and algebra-valued cohomology/local/Selmer functors, and specifies Kim’s representability, invariant-coset, localization and dimension arguments. Geometric supplier contracts, all-algebra descent and local closedness are explicit open inputs; this packet does not claim a closed or implemented stage.

nodes.title: Canonical additive comparison
nodes.statement: For a continuous G-action on an additive topological abelian group M, use the parent comparison α: H1(G,Multiplicative M) ≃ ContCohomology.H1 G M induced by c↦toAdd∘c, with α(1)=0. For a compatible pair φ:H→G and continuous additive f:M→N, α_H,N∘(φ,f)_*=explicitMap1(φ,f)∘α_G,M. On cocycles the gauge by m translates by −d0(m); hence the quotient comparison is independent of the sign of the B1 generator. The comparison is the identity on underlying cocycle functions, not an arbitrary bijection.
hypotheses: M,N topological additive abelian groups with jointly continuous automorphism actions
φ continuous homomorphism and f continuous additive equivariant for φ.
proofSteps: Use the accepted parent cocycle equivalence and H1 quotient equivalence.
Read the explicitMap1 representative formula and compare both composites at every h∈H.
Use class-map surjectivity for equality on H1; check gauge m becomes m+c−g·m.
acceptance: The neutral class maps to zero; cocycle representatives remain unchanged after writing the operation additively.

nodes.title: Abelian finite-quotient transport
nodes.statement: For profinite G (compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected) and discrete additive M with continuous G-action, the canonical comparisons identify parent nonabelian descent, inflation and reverse-inclusion transition H1(G/U,(Multiplicative M)^U)→H1(G/V,(Multiplicative M)^V), V≤U, with Tau Ceti descendZ1, explicitInfl1 and explicitFiniteQuotientTransition1, after the canonical invariant-coefficient identification. They induce the comparison of the Set-colimit with the underlying set of the apex of explicitFiniteQuotientCocone1, namely Tau Ceti H1 G M. The declaration explicitFiniteQuotientColimit1 is the IsColimit certificate for this named cocone. Descent requires a representative pointwise neutral on U; neutral restriction of its class alone first requires a gauge correction.
hypotheses: G profinite (compact Hausdorff totally disconnected) topological group
M discrete topological additive abelian group
proofSteps: Identify invariant coefficients by unchanged underlying values and their native induced topologies.
Apply canonical-comparison-naturality to the quotient homomorphisms and invariant inclusions.
Evaluate descended cocycles on quotient representatives and use the parent killing/descent theorem.

Transport the parent Type-valued inflation cocone to the underlying cocone with apex Tau Ceti H1 G M. The reverse-inclusion index is filtered, so forgetting additive groups preserves this colimit; explicitFiniteQuotientColimit1 certifies universality, rather than naming another carrier.
acceptance: The transition for U=V is identity; a finer level inflates to the same global class; no discrete-coefficient theorem is invoked for Qp.

nodes.title: Positive central defect
nodes.statement: For topological groups G,B with continuous G-action by automorphisms and a function b:G→B define D_b(g,h)=b(g)·g(b(h))·b(gh)−1 in that order. It is continuous if b is continuous. If q:B→C is an equivariant homomorphism and q∘b is a cocycle then D_b takes values in ker(q).
proofSteps: Form the displayed product using multiplication, inverse, action and group multiplication.
Apply q, the cocycle law and cancellation to prove the kernel assertion.
For cocycle tests use D=1 iff the multiplicative cocycle law.
acceptance: Positive defect becomes d1 in an additive central group.

nodes.title: Continuous central H2 bridge
nodes.statement: Let i:Multiplicative M→B be injective, equivariant and central. If a continuous f:G×G→M satisfies i(ofAdd(f(g,h)))=D_b(g,h), then f lies in ContCohomology.Z2 G M. Replacing b by i(ofAdd(a(g)))b(g), for a continuous a:G→M, changes f by d1(a). Therefore its actual continuous H2 class is unchanged.
proofSteps: Expand the associative triple product b(g)g(b(h))gh(b(k)) in the two parenthesizations.
Move central defects past b(g), obtaining g·f(h,k)−f(gh,k)+f(g,hk)−f(g,h)=0; use mem_Z2_iff.
For the changed lift expand D and use centrality to identify the difference with d1(a).
Use mem_B2_iff and H2pi_eq_iff; continuity of a is indispensable.
acceptance: A discontinuous primitive does not prove equality in this H2; positive and source inverse defects have opposite additive classes.

nodes.title: Continuous lift exactness
nodes.statement: In the preceding central situation, [f]=0 in continuous H2 iff there is a continuous a:G→M such that i(ofAdd(a(g)))b(g) is a cocycle. If q∘b=c and q∘i=1, that corrected cocycle is a continuous lift of c. Conversely every continuous lift differs from b by a continuous M-valued cochain provided i is a homeomorphism onto ker(q).
hypotheses: b continuous and i continuous for the corrected lift
homeomorphism onto ker(q) for the converse concerning arbitrary lifts.
proofSteps: Use H2pi_eq_zero_iff and mem_B2_iff to write f=d1(t) with continuous t.
Choose a=−t and apply the positive lift-change formula.
For a different continuous lift, identify its pointwise ratio with M through the continuous inverse of i; this supplies a continuous primitive.
acceptance: The correction has sign −t; its quotient cocycle is unchanged.

sources.locator: Section 1, Proposition 2 obstruction induction, printed pp. 7–9

nodes.title: Obstruction on gauge classes
nodes.statement: For a central G-equivariant exact sequence 1→Multiplicative M→B→C→1 with the kernel identification a homeomorphism, q surjective and a continuous set section, D_{s∘c} defines δ:H1(G,C)→ContCohomology.H2 G M. It is independent of the section and of the cocycle representative. Its zero fibre is the image of H1(G,B), and δ is natural for continuous equivariant morphisms of such central sequences. The inverse source convention changes δ to −δ without changing the zero fibre.
hypotheses: Topological groups and continuous automorphism actions
central kernel identification continuous both ways
proofSteps: Compare two continuous lifts using the kernel homeomorphism and continuous-central-obstruction.
For a gauge element in C choose a lift in B by surjectivity; gauge the B-valued lift and use centrality to show its central defect is unchanged.
Apply central-lift-exactness and the accepted parent quotient-class map.
Under a morphism compare defects on representatives and then pass to continuous H2.
acceptance: A choice of an algebraic section supplies continuity only after the point-topology theorem; exactness is not inferred from an orbit-fibre theorem lacking H2.

nodes.title: Invariant orbit transport
nodes.statement: For a surjective continuous equivariant f:U→V and c∈Z1(G,U), let K_c be the native kernel in the inner twist and A_c=H0(G,V_{f∘c}). Transport the parent A_c-action along its named-kernel or embedded-kernel H1 equivalence E, defining v·a=E−1(v·E(a)). E is orbit-equivariant and induces an equivalence of actual orbit quotients with the fibre f_*−1([f∘c]); its representative maps to [g↦i(d(g))c(g)]. Inclusion squares, stabilizers and conjugate actions under change of c commute. No equality of kernel classes is claimed when only invariant orbits agree.
hypotheses: Parent native action, orbit-fibre equivalence and kernel homeomorphisms
embedded i retains its given topology
proofSteps: Use the parent actual E and its inverse to transport the action and prove the action laws.
Use E equivariance for orbit and stabilizer equivalences and the parent inclusion triangle for the fibre map.
For a representative change c′=u·c, conjugation by u identifies the two twists, kernels and invariant groups; compare representatives with the gauge law.
acceptance: Transported stabilizers equal native stabilizers; the orbit of the neutral kernel class maps to [c], which can be nonneutral.

nodes.title: Galois coefficient family
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring K and topological group G, a GaloisCoefficientFamily P assigns to each commutative K-algebra R a topological group P(R) with jointly continuous G-action by automorphisms. Each algebra map f:R→S gives a continuous equivariant group homomorphism P(f), with identity and composition laws. This packages the family supplied by actual unipotent points; it does not assert any algebraicity or representability.
hypotheses: a fixed universe for coefficient algebras and point types.
proofSteps: Use native CommAlgCat for coefficient changes.
Bundle group and topology structures, continuous action, continuous group maps and their equivariance/functor laws.
Geometric instantiation requires unipotent-point-topology.
acceptance: For trivial G-action, Z1 is the set of continuous homomorphisms, while H1 is its quotient by constant conjugation. The interface never substitutes Hom for this gauge quotient.

sources.locator: Section 1, Lemmas 1–5, printed pp. 2–4
sources.match: Algebra-valued points have continuous group operations, coefficient maps and semilinear G-actions.

nodes.title: Continuous unipotent points
nodes.statement: Instantiate GaloisCoefficientFamily by P_n(R)=U_n(B⊗_K R), using the native smooth-unipotent Hopf/group-scheme dictionary, a finite-type filtered G-stable coordinate Hopf algebra and its polynomial point charts. Here B is a complete Hausdorff characteristic-zero topological field with continuous semilinear G-action, K⊂F=B^G and [F:K]<∞. Put the final topology on B⊗_K R from its finite-dimensional B-subspaces. The chart topology is independent of the embedding, polynomial maps and coefficient changes are continuous, and G×P_n(R)→P_n(R) is jointly continuous. Central vector quotient sections that are regular maps are continuous on points.
hypotheses: B complete Hausdorff topological field with continuous field automorphism action
K is a subfield of F=B^G and [F:K]<∞.
finite-type filtered Hopf coordinates with finite-rank G-stable filtration and compatible semilinear action.
proofSteps: Use the native Hopf/group-scheme dictionary, retaining its smooth-unipotent object rather than replacing it.
Prove chart independence by polynomial transition maps and continuity on each finite-dimensional coefficient subspace, as in Lemmas 1–3.
Use a finite-dimensional G-stable generating filtration and continuity of its coefficient action to prove joint action continuity, as in Lemma 5.
Import central vector quotients and regular sections from the unipotent group supplier; pointwise surjectivity alone is insufficient.
acceptance: An arbitrary change of an algebraic chart gives the same topology; the NC.2 depth tower is lower-central, not the augmentation-length tower.

sources.locator: Section 1, Lemmas 1–3 and 5, printed pp. 2–4
sources.match: The finite-dimensional coefficient topology makes algebraic point operations and G-actions continuous.

proofSteps: Apply the parent continuous equivariant coefficient pushforward to each P(f).
Check functor laws on representatives and pass to gauge classes.
Use the parent class-map surjectivity to prove natural identities.

nodes.title: Cochain scalar extension
nodes.statement: For a finite-dimensional B-vector G-module V of the specified semilinear type and every K-algebra R with the finite-subspace final topology, the canonical map C^j_cont(G,V)⊗_K R→C^j_cont(G,V⊗_K R) is an isomorphism for j=0,1,2,3, compatible with differentials. Consequently continuous Z1, B1 and H1 commute with this scalar extension; H2 has the analogous comparison. H^j(G,V) is considered over K through F=B^G. Compact image containment in a finite-dimensional coefficient subspace is an explicit required input, not a property of arbitrary tensor-product topologies.
hypotheses: every continuous map from G^j into V⊗R has image in a finite-dimensional B-subspace generated by finitely many R-coefficients.
proofSteps: For surjectivity use compactness plus the specified compact-image lemma to expand a continuous cochain in finitely many coefficient coordinates.
For injectivity choose a finite linearly independent K-coefficient list and use coordinate projections; check continuity of the projections in the final topology.
Identify the differentials termwise; scalar extension over a field is exact, so kernels, images and quotients agree.
acceptance: For R=K the comparison is identity; for dual numbers K[ε]/ε² it retains both coefficient components; no unrestricted topological tensor assertion is made.

sources.locator: Section 1, Lemma 4 printed p. 3; Proposition 2 vector base case printed pp. 7–8
sources.match: The compact-image argument makes the continuous vector cochain complex commute with coefficient algebra extension.

nodes.title: Filtered affine torsor comparison
nodes.statement: For filtered finite-type unipotent U_n over B⊗_K R, classify equivariant affine right U_n-torsors whose coordinate rings have an exhaustive filtration by finite-rank locally free pieces of the same ranks as the corresponding pieces of the group coordinate ring. Require the filtration inclusions to be locally split and universally injective, the torsor coaction to preserve the filtration, and the semilinear G-action on each finite piece to be continuous. Isomorphisms are equivariant filtered affine torsor isomorphisms. Under the supplier theorem that split-unipotent fppf torsors over this affine coefficient base have a point and admit a strict filtered trivialization, evaluation at a point gives a natural bijection of their isomorphism classes with H1(G,U_n(B⊗R)). Coefficient-base descent and the reconstruction by a cocycle must be effective in this filtered affine category; a nonempty topological torsor bijection alone does not establish these facts.
hypotheses: Exhaustive locally free finite-rank filtration pieces, locally split universally injective inclusions, and filtration-compatible torsor coaction.
supplied affine torsor triviality, compatible filtered trivialization and effective descent.
proofSteps: Apply supplier affine unipotent torsor triviality, obtained by induction through vector groups and vanishing of affine quasi-coherent H1.
Use a point to identify the underlying affine right torsor with U_n and verify strict filtration.
Construct the cocycle from the semilinear G-action using unipotent-point-topology; reconstruct the filtered affine torsor by twisting the Hopf coaction.
Compare the affine construction on points with the accepted parent torsor classification and verify descent of algebra morphisms.
acceptance: An empty point space is excluded only after the affine triviality theorem; filtered algebra isomorphism must be proved, not inferred from a homeomorphism.

sources.locator: Section 1, filtered torsor definition and Proposition 1, printed pp. 4–7
sources.match: The source classification uses affine filtered torsors; continuity of a nonempty point torsor is only one of its ingredients.

nodes.title: Finite-level representability
nodes.statement: Let U_n be a finite-depth tower of characteristic-zero smooth split unipotent groups over B, with central vector layers V_i, regular sections of U_{i+1}→U_i, continuous semilinear G-action and the coefficient topology above. Assume [B^G:K]<∞, finite-dimensional K-vector H^j_cont(G,V_i(B)) for j=0,1,2, and H0(G,V_i(B))=0 for every i. Then R↦H1(G,U_n(B⊗_K R)) is corepresented by a finitely generated commutative K-algebra. At each extension the positive obstruction gives a morphism δ_i:H1(U_i)→H2(V_i); its scheme-theoretic zero fibre I_i is closed affine, and a noncanonical universal choice of continuous primitive gives H1(U_{i+1})≅H1(V_i)×I_i as functors of all K-algebras. The inverse-depth limit is an affine proalgebraic functor.
proofSteps: At depth one use canonical-comparison-naturality and cochain-scalar-extension to obtain the affine vector space H1(G,V_1).
Inductively choose the universal cocycle over the representing algebra; construct its positive continuous central obstruction in the finite-dimensional H2 vector space.
Form the scheme-theoretic zero fibre, retaining nilpotent algebra points. Split the linear map C1→B2 on its image, so a universal obstruction-zero class has a continuous lift.
Twisted invariants of U_i vanish by induction from vanishing graded H0. The parent central H1 action is consequently free, giving the product with H1(V_i).
The product and zero fibre are affine finite type. Transition morphisms supply the affine proalgebraic limit.
acceptance: If H2=0, the next level is a product with H1(V_i); if δ is nonzero its zero fibre is retained; neither vanishing H2 nor smoothness of I_i is assumed.

sources.locator: Section 1, Proposition 2 and its induction, printed pp. 7–9
sources.match: Finite vector cohomology, vanishing invariants and central vector lifts give the represented affine cohomology functor.

nodes.title: Invariant coset representability
nodes.statement: Suppose U is as above and defined over K, with the G-stable subgroup U_n(R)⊂U_n(B⊗_K R) and a closed topological embedding on these points for each R. The quotient here is the coset G-set of elements bH, even when the subgroup is nonnormal. With continuous vector-quotient cochains commuting with coefficient extension and finite-dimensional K-vector invariants and H1 for W_i=V_i(B)/V_i(K), the functor R↦H0(G,U_n(B⊗R)/U_n(R)) is affine finite type. In the central induction its kernel is H0(G,W_i⊗_K R) and its image is I_i=ker(ob_i) inside the previous invariant-coset variety, with ob_i landing in H1(G,W_i). A choice of universal section yields the product H0(G,W_i)×I_i.
hypotheses: K-defined tower, with G-stable U_n(R) and a closed topological embedding U_n(R)→U_n(B⊗_K R) for every R; verify this in the chosen final topologies.
left-coset action on bH, not quotient group
central lifting and effectiveness of coset construction.
proofSteps: Use the parent nonnormal invariant-coset connecting construction to define ob_i. Retain its closed-embedding hypothesis, which supplies continuous recovery of the kernel-valued cocycle.
Identify the central vector kernel W_i and use quotient-cochain scalar extension.
Take the zero fibre of the vector obstruction and construct a universal lift by splitting vector coboundaries.
Identify each fibre as a torsor under H0(W_i); obtain the product after choosing its universal section.
acceptance: For U=V additive the answer is H0(G,V(B)/V(K)); for B=K the quotient is a point; never require U_n(R) normal.

nodes.title: Local neutral locus
nodes.statement: For set-valued algebra functors F,T, a natural transformation f:F→T and a natural neutral point e of T, define neutralLocus(R)={x∈F(R):f_R(x)=e_R}. Its algebra maps are restrictions of F maps. For an inertia restriction map this gives H1_un; for extension of coefficients Qp→B_dR or Qp→B_cris it gives H1_g or H1_f respectively, once the actual continuous cohomology functors are supplied. The definition uses every coefficient algebra R; it asserts no representability or closedness.
proofSteps: Form the fibre subtype over the natural neutral point.
Naturality preserves membership under each coefficient map.
Use subtype extensionality for functor laws and universal factoring of neutralized maps.
acceptance: BDR-neutralization is H1_g; crystalline neutralization is H1_f and implies H1_g through Bcris→BDR.

nodes.title: Local condition geometry
nodes.statement: For the geometric étale U_n over a local field k_v/Qp, use finite-level-representability to represent local H1. Assume finite vector cohomology and the stated invariant vanishing on every central layer, actual period-ring topologies, and effective filtered-torsor/coset descent over every coefficient algebra. In the central product chart H1(V_i)×I_i, assume the lower local condition cuts out a represented closed base J_i⊂I_i and that universal quotient neutralizations yield finitely many natural defect maps to vector spaces W_ij: the next local condition on (x,y) is exactly ell_ij(x)+b_ij(y)=0, for all algebras, where ell_ij is linear and b_ij is natural in J_i. Then induction represents the crystalline neutralLocus by a closed affine finite-type subfunctor. The invariant-coset boundary has this functor as its pointwise image only with effective coset lifting and descent on all algebras; no field-point image substitutes for this assertion. The same criterion constructs fixed unramified and fixed finite-index H_v conditions. For unramifiedness use the revised central induction through vector inertia conditions; do not assume H1(I_v,U_n) is represented by a variety.
hypotheses: Local k_v finite over Qp, finite depth, and the finite-level representability hypotheses.
Actual period coefficient actions/topologies; B_cris is not treated as the complete topological field in Kim2005.
Fixed inertia or specified finite-index subgroup H_v; vector neutral conditions and detection spaces W_ij are finite-dimensional and commute with coefficient extension.
Effective invariant-coset and strictly filtered torsor descent, including universal quotient neutralizations over each J_i.
The displayed affine-linear defect criterion is proved on all algebras and is independent of chosen neutralization after passing to cohomology.
proofSteps: Form local-neutral-locus with the actual inertia/period maps; Bcris→BDR gives H1_f⊂H1_g.
Apply the period analogue of invariant-coset-representability only after its topology and effective quotient hypotheses have been proved; the field theorem alone does not cover Bcris.
Use central-lift-exactness and effective filtered torsors to identify the invariant-coset boundary image with the neutralization functor on every algebra.

Over the closed base J_i, a universal quotient neutralization reduces the next condition to the finite vector equations ell_ij(x)+b_ij(y)=0. Yoneda represents b_ij by a morphism to its vector scheme, and these equations give closed zero fibres.

For inertia, repeat this argument with the vector restrictions. The corrected Kim2009 argument does not require finite-type representability of the full nonabelian inertia target. Verify the universal-neutralization criterion for the geometric tower under G3.
acceptance: Keep H1_f distinct from H1_g; if inertia acts trivially a neutral restricted class has representative identically one; potential conditions use a fixed H_v, not an uncontrolled union.

nodes.title: Selmer functor
nodes.statement: Given the global algebra functor F_T(R)=H1(G_{k,T},U_n(R)), a finite set of local indices Σ including all chosen bad and p-adic places, local functors L_v, localization natural transformations r_v and coefficient-stable subsets C_v(R), define Sel_T(U_n)(R)={x∈F_T(R):r_v(x)∈C_v(R) for every v∈Σ}. At good places outside T unramifiedness is already in G_{k,T}; at bad places retain the specified local conditions, and at p use crystalline neutralization where its hypotheses apply.
hypotheses: finite T containing p, infinity and ramified coefficient places
finite Σ with fixed local conditions
proofSteps: Take the intersection of the pullback subfunctors using the displayed actual localization maps.
Coefficient stability gives a functor; inclusion and localizations are restrictions of global maps.
Functors on arbitrary algebras distinguish a represented scheme from its k-points.
acceptance: A class failing one bad-place condition fails the Selmer condition even if it is crystalline at p.

nodes.title: Selmer representability
nodes.statement: If the global F_T and each local L_v are represented affine finite type over Qp, their localization natural transformations are represented morphisms, and each C_v is a represented closed subfunctor for the fixed finite Σ, then Sel_T(U_n) is the iterated fibre product of F_T with all C_v over all L_v, hence a closed affine finite-type scheme. Its functor of all commutative Qp-algebras is exactly selmerFunctor, including nilpotent coefficients.
hypotheses: hypotheses just stated supplied by finite-level-representability and local-condition-geometry
native scheme fibre products and closed immersions.
proofSteps: Use Yoneda to turn the localization natural transformations into morphisms of the representing affine schemes.
Take a finite product of local morphisms and pull back the closed product of local subfunctors.
Verify the functor-of-points universal property on every coefficient algebra, then finite type and affineness.
acceptance: Dual-number points satisfy the same local conditions; rational-point intersections alone are insufficient.

nodes.title: Localization and depth functoriality
nodes.statement: For equivariant morphisms of the geometric unipotent towers preserving every chosen local condition, all depth projections and coefficient maps induce Selmer morphisms, commute with localization, preserve neutral classes and compose correctly. Enlarging T compares global groups through the actual quotient homomorphism G_{k,T′}→G_{k,T}; it does not discard local conditions at newly permitted bad places. The central positive obstruction commutes with localization and coefficient change.
hypotheses: Geometric tower maps equivariant and continuous
proofSteps: Use parent functoriality and canonical-comparison-naturality for global/local classes.
Check condition preservation place by place; restrict transformations to selmerFunctor.
Use Yoneda for represented morphisms and central-obstruction-descent for the obstruction square.
acceptance: The p-localization square agrees on representatives; a newly ramified place still appears among the conditions.

nodes.title: Central Selmer dimension bound
nodes.statement: For a central vector sequence 1→V→U_{n+1}→U_n→1, suppose the Selmer functors and depth map are represented by finite-type schemes. Require the global H1(V)-action and difference classification on all coefficient algebras and after field extension, with all corresponding twisted quotient invariants trivial so that this action is free. Require addition by a linear Selmer class to preserve every local condition, and the unique difference of two Selmer lifts to satisfy exactly those linear conditions, on all these algebras. At p this requires surjectivity U_{n+1}(B_cris⊗R)^{H_v}→U_n(B_cris⊗R)^{H_v} on the relevant invariant points, with their actual crystalline comparison; at fixed unramified places use the analogous inertia difference calculation. Then every nonempty geometric fibre is a torsor under the vector scheme Sel_T(V). After choosing a point it is isomorphic to that vector scheme on all algebras over the geometric residue field. Consequently dim Sel_T(U_{n+1})≤dim Sel_T(U_n)+dim_Qp Sel_T(V); the obstruction zero fibre can make the inequality strict.
hypotheses: Central vector sequence and represented finite-type Selmer schemes and depth morphism.
The global central H1 action, orbit classification and vanishing twisted invariants hold over every coefficient algebra and remain valid after field extension.
Local addition and difference conditions agree exactly with linear Selmer conditions on all those algebras.
Invariant crystalline lifting for every relevant B_cris⊗R and fixed H_v, and the analogous fixed unramified difference theorem.
Sel_T(V) is the finite-dimensional vector Selmer functor, with scalar extension to the geometric residue fields.
proofSteps: The parent central extension identifies global fibres as H1(V)-orbits; vanishing twisted invariants makes the action free.

For two local crystalline lifts, compare period trivializations and lift their quotient invariant through the specified surjective invariant map; the resulting vector difference is crystalline. Its invariant realization is crystalline U_cr over the absolutely unramified field; U_DR is obtained after scalar extension, as recorded in E5.
At fixed unramified places use the actual inertia restriction; for trivial inertia action neutral means the vector cocycle is zero.

Addition by a linear Selmer class preserves the local conditions. After a point of a geometric fibre is chosen, the all-algebra action/difference identities give inverse natural maps between that fibre functor and the vector Selmer functor. Yoneda makes this a scheme isomorphism; a bijection merely on field-valued points would not suffice.
Apply the finite-type scheme fibre-dimension inequality, not a dimension field stored as an assumption.
acceptance: At depth one the bound reduces to the linear Selmer dimension; no equality or smoothness of all fibres is asserted; local invariant surjectivity cannot be omitted.

nodes.title: Depth-one Kummer and Selmer comparison
nodes.statement: For the geometric U_1 supplied by NC.2, identify it with the vector realization of the abelianized geometric fundamental group, using NC.2’s Jacobian/Tate-module conventions (and its puncture contribution for an open curve). The canonical additive H1 comparison intertwines global restriction, local unramified/crystalline conditions and the resulting linear Selmer subgroup. For a proper curve and its Jacobian J this is the rational Tate-module Selmer space with the actual Kummer map from J(k)⊗Qp; path classes of [x−b] agree with that map under the NC.2 comparison. Do not replace rational p-adic Selmer by a finite μ_m Selmer group.
hypotheses: Number field curve with rational basepoint
proper curve for pure Jacobian statement
actual p-adic Kummer and local realization comparisons.
proofSteps: Use NC.2 depth-one-jacobian to fix dual and Tate-twist conventions, and separate puncture terms for affine curves.
Apply canonical-comparison-naturality to every global/local map, then equality of local neutral loci.
Import the NC.2 path/Kummer identification and the linear Selmer owner’s local rational Jacobian Kummer comparison; compare all class and localization maps.
acceptance: For the identity Jacobian point the path class is neutral; depth-one classes obey the identical local conditions; boundary Tate terms are retained for an open curve.

nodes.title: A nonzero depth-two obstruction
nodes.statement: Let X,Y,Z be continuous topological additive G-modules and β:X×Y→Z a continuous G-equivariant bilinear pairing. The Heisenberg extension U=X×Y×Z has law (x,y,z)(x′,y′,z′)=(x+x′,y+y′,z+z′+β(x,y′)). For cocycles a∈Z1(G,X), b∈Z1(G,Y), the section g↦(a(g),b(g),0) has positive defect β(a(g),g·b(h)); its H2 class is the oriented cup product [a]∪_β[b]. It lifts iff that class is zero. For actual local Galois G=G_k with k/Qp finite, X=Qp, Y=Z=Qp(1) and the scalar pairing, local Tate duality supplies a,b with nonzero cup product in H2(G_k,Qp(1))≃Qp; that depth-two class does not lift. This example tests obstruction theory, not the H0-vanishing representability hypothesis, since X has nonzero invariants.
hypotheses: local p-adic duality with nonzero H1(Qp) for the nonzero Galois specialization.
proofSteps: Use bilinearity for associativity, inverse and central kernel; the projection to X×Y is split by z=0 as a continuous set map.
Evaluate positiveDefect and identify β(a(g),g·b(h)); use continuous-central-obstruction and central-lift-exactness.

Import the continuous cup convention and rational local Tate duality. For V=Qp, H0 has dimension 1 and H2 is dual to H0(Qp(1))=0; the local Euler characteristic therefore gives dim H1(Qp)=1+[k:Qp]>0. Choose a nonzero class and a dual Qp(1) class with nonzero pairing, identified by the local invariant with H2(Qp(1))≃Qp.

As a separate explicit sign check take discrete G=Z², X=Y=Z=Q, trivial action and coordinate homomorphisms. The two-cochain m(g)n(h) is not a coboundary because all trivial-action one-cochain coboundaries on abelian G are symmetric, while it takes 1 and 0 on the swapped coordinate generators.
acceptance: The cup order is a(g) paired with g·b(h); swapping source sign negates its H2 class but preserves nonliftability; the actual Galois example requires the already planned rational p-adic duality supplier and the requested continuous cup-convention comparison.

requests.need: Native functor-of-points and fppf torsor descent/effectivity for finite-type filtered affine group schemes over arbitrary characteristic-zero coefficient algebras; represented finite products, zero fibres and Yoneda maps preserving all algebra points.

Coset fppf quotient on bH and effective descent for possibly nonnormal subgroup inclusions; compatibility with actual R-point cosets and central vector kernels under stated lifting hypotheses. Do not identify sheaf quotient points with naive R-cosets without proof.

Characteristic-zero split smooth unipotent central quotients are vector groups, projection torsors over affine bases admit regular set sections, and split-unipotent fppf torsors over affine coefficient bases are trivial, by vector induction; compatible filtered trivializations where used.

For actual finite-dimensional continuous Qp geometric G_{k,T} and G_v representations, prove global finite-dimensional H0,H1,H2 over Qp, localization and the precise arithmetic hypotheses needed for graded invariant vanishings. Use the existing D7/local-coefficient-field-duality and D7/local-invariant-trivialization nodes for local rational duality rather than replanning them; finite-module Taylor–Wiles finiteness is insufficient for the global geometric representations.

Native B_cris and B_dR coefficient rings, G_v-actions and continuous point base extension on filtered finite unipotent groups, with the inclusion B_cris→B_dR and quotient cochain base-change/compact-image inputs needed for invariant cosets. B_cris is not silently treated as the complete field B of Kim2005.

Period-admissibility inputs ensuring local crystalline vector subspaces and invariant-lift surjectivity for the specific central geometric extensions, after the fixed H_v restriction. Supply exact hypotheses, not the assertion that all extensions of crystalline objects have crystalline cocycle classes. Prove the invariant-lifting and local addition/difference criteria for B_cris⊗R on every coefficient algebra and after residue-field extension; identify the invariants through U_cr over K0 before de Rham base change.

Generalize the existing L4/elliptic-finite-kummer local rational Kummer comparison to the Jacobian of an arbitrary proper curve, with the exact global rational Selmer limit. NC.2/depth-one-jacobian already supplies the geometric path/Kummer identification; import it instead of replanning it. Finite μ_m descent alone is insufficient.

Continuous Qp-valued low-degree cup products for non-discrete representations and the equivariant bilinear formula (a∪b)(g,h)=β(a(g),g·b(h)), compatible with the explicit positive H2 quotient. Import the existing D7 continuous cohomology direction; the required extra input is comparison of its cup convention with Tau Ceti’s explicit low-degree quotient, not a second general cup-product theory.

gaps.title: G1 — Compact-image and quotient-cochain topology
gaps.detail: Prove the compact-image finite-coefficient lemma for the exact final topologies used, including vector period quotients. Kim2005 Lemma 4 motivates the field case; the proof obligations for B_cris quotients and arbitrary algebras are not supplied by discrete ProfiniteCohomology. Include the finite-product final-topology and polynomial continuity lemmas needed to instantiate the coefficient family.

gaps.title: G2 — Filtered algebraic torsor and coset effectivity
gaps.detail: Supplier group-scheme triviality, strict filtered trivialization and descent must be verified over every coefficient algebra; parent nonempty topological torsor classification is insufficient. Relate naive point cosets to the effective quotient used in representability. Verify locally free filtration pieces and locally split universally injective inclusions, and the closed point embeddings required by the imported coset connecting map.

gaps.title: G3 — Closed crystalline loci and local fibre compatibility
gaps.detail: Establish an effective all-algebra invariant-coset image and a central induction proving represented closed local loci, together with actual local invariant-lift surjectivity for the geometric tower. A morphism image need not be closed and an image on field points need not describe all algebra points; neither claim is inferred without proof. In particular construct universal quotient neutralizations and the finite affine-linear local defect criterion on each central product chart; use the revised inertia induction. Prove local addition/difference and crystalline invariant lifting after arbitrary coefficient and residue-field extension, not just on Qp-points.

gaps.title: G4 — Native geometric and inherited prototype signatures
gaps.detail: The suggested file elaborates concrete central-defect, family, H1, neutral-locus and Selmer functor signatures against the pin. Remaining named geometric theorems and inherited twist/diagram comparisons are omitted individually under PROTOCOL section 13 until their native supplier interfaces are assembled. The reader and packet state their mathematics exactly; no arbitrary Prop field substitutes for them.

Assemble native inherited twist/finite-quotient and filtered Hopf/period interfaces and add the fourteen individually identified omitted signatures (G4).
Apply the independently reviewed obstruction and cup conventions while verifying all geometric supplier hypotheses. Acceptance of this planning pass leaves G1–G4 open; it does not mark NC.3 closed.

checked.note: The identity on additive representatives sends the chosen gauge to subtraction of d0; the actual compatible-pair formula is f(c(φh)). Restriction, coefficients and neutral elements commute.

Replaced the nonexistent carrier of an IsColimit certificate with the named cocone apex H1 G M and added its pinned definition. Checked transition direction and pointwise descent versus gauge-normalized neutral restriction.
Ordered multiplication gives the positive defect; it is continuous, maps to the kernel, equals b(1) at (1,1), and converts to the pinned positive d1. All four APIs and sign/order tests match.
Associativity and centrality give d2=0. Changing lift by i(a) adds d1 a, so the continuous B2 quotient gives lift independence. The Lean signature uses an actual continuous kernel cochain.
H2pi=0 is exactly existence of a continuous primitive. Correction by its negative gives a cocycle; arbitrary lift differences need the explicitly stated kernel homeomorphism for continuity.

A continuous section and the central kernel homeomorphism recover continuous cochains. Lifting a constant gauge proves representative independence; compatible pairs prove naturality, and the zero fibre is exactly the image. The full signature remains honestly omitted under G4.

Transport through the parent named/embedded kernel equivalence conjugates the actual invariant action and its stabilizers. Translation d(g)c(g) targets the fibre over [c], and classifies orbits rather than unique kernel classes.

Native topological groups, jointly continuous automorphism actions, and continuous equivariant coefficient homomorphisms are correctly bundled. Added a composition test and corrected the downstream source locator; structural projections are existing API. Clarified that trivial action identifies Z1 with homomorphisms, whereas H1 still quotients by conjugation.

Clarified the direction and degree of K⊂B^G. The native unipotent category is consumed, not replanned. Added its final-topology product/polynomial obligations to G1; no field theorem is applied to Bcris.

The carrier is the actual gauge quotient and coefficient maps act on representatives. Added a representative test excluding maps that only preserve gauges and the neutral class; source use now points to published section 4.

The cochain tensor map requires compact-image finite coefficient containment and continuous coordinate projections. Exact tensoring over a field then carries kernels, boundaries and cohomology through degrees 1 and 2. G1 retains the period-quotient obligation.

Specified locally free finite filtration pieces with matching piece ranks, locally split universally injective inclusions, and compatible coaction. Strict affine trivialization and effective descent remain supplied hypotheses in G2.

With the stated scalar-extension and graded H0 hypotheses, the universal obstruction gives a closed zero fibre. A continuous universal primitive and freeness give a noncanonical H1(vector) product on all algebras. Finite depth is finite type; the inverse system is proalgebraic.

Retained the closed point-embedding hypothesis of the imported connecting map. The quotient is the nonnormal coset G-set bH; its central invariant factor is H0(vector quotient), as in inherited E1, and its obstruction is in H1 of that vector quotient.

The concrete subtype and coefficient maps express neutralization on every algebra; membership, injection and unique factorization are correct. Changed the Lean extensionality signature to the packet’s iff and replaced the source locator with the version of record.

Replaced vague stable local conditions by an explicit universal affine-linear vector defect criterion proving closedness. Switched to the published revised inertia induction, retained effective all-algebra image/descent, and kept Bcris outside the field case. G3 is still open.

The actual subtype imposes every specified local condition and maps by coefficient stability. Strengthened empty/universal tests to require the equivalence to be the actual inclusion, and corrected the published section/page locator.

Finite fibre products of represented closed local subfunctors give the claimed closed affine finite-type scheme on all algebras, including nilpotents. Corrected its source locator; no field-point intersection is used as a scheme proof.

Representative maps commute with local restriction, coefficients and central obstruction. Enlarging ramification uses G_Tprime→G_T while preserving the new local conditions. Corrected source locators; no mathematics was replaced.

Removed the geometric fibre torsor conclusion from the hypotheses. Required the all-algebra global action, local differences and invariant lifting, then used a chosen geometric point and Yoneda to obtain the vector-scheme fibre. Distinguished U_cr invariants from U_DR base change (E5) and corrected the locator to pp. 128–129.

NC.2 supplies the geometric Jacobian/Tate path comparison; the additive comparison preserves the precise rational local conditions, and the existing request retains rational Jacobian Kummer input. The proper/open distinction is sound; source locator corrected.

The Heisenberg positive defect is β(a(g),g·b(h)). Made nonzero H1(Qp) explicit using the supplier’s Euler characteristic, and distinguished the existing rational duality theorem from the requested cup-convention comparison. The nonliftable example is not an H0-vanishing representability example; source locator corrected.
